The issue is confirmed: the `ExportButton` component does not re-enable after a failed export because the `handleClick` function only calls `setBusy(false)` in the `.then()` block, which is never executed if `exportReport` throws an error (e.g., due to a failed API response). The button remains disabled until a page reload. The fix requires catching the error in `exportReport` and resetting `busy` to `false` in the `.catch()` block.

input.title: Re-enable ExportButton after failed export by resetting busy state
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `busy` state is only reset in the success path of `exportReport` (inside `.then()`), but not in the failure path. If the export fails (e.g., due to a server error), the `busy` state remains `true`, disabling the button permanently until a page reload. The fix is to reset `setBusy(false)` in the `.catch()` block of the `exportReport` call, ensuring the button is re-enabled after any export attempt, successful or not.
